The '''2018–19 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] in the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]].  They were led by eighth-year head coach [[Mark Turgeon]], and played their home games at [[Xfinity Center (College Park, Maryland)|Xfinity Center]] in [[College Park, Maryland]], as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. They finished the season 23–11, 13–7 in [[2018–19 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in fifth place. They lost in the second round of the [[2019 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] to [[2018–19 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 6 seed in the East region. There they defeated [[2018–19 Belmont Bruins men's basketball team|Belmont]] before losing to [[2018–19 LSU Tigers basketball team|LSU]] in the second round.

==Previous season==
The [[2017–18 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Terrapins]] finished the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]] 19–13, 8–10 in [[2017–18 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in eighth place. They lost in the second round of the [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] to [[2017–18 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/maryland-basketball-finds-familiar-bitter-end-vs-wisconsin-in-big-ten-tournament/2018/03/01/0a21b942-1d77-11e8-ae5a-16e60e4605f3_story.html|title=In the end, this Maryland basketball season is defined by a bungled inbounds play|last=Stubbs|first=Roman|date=2018-03-01|work=Washington Post|access-date=2018-06-05|language=en-US|issn=0190-8286}}</ref> They were invited to the [[College Basketball Invitational]], but declined, marking their absence in a postseason tournament for the first time since [[2013–14 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|2014]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.testudotimes.com/2012/3/11/2863397/maryland-misses-nit-for-second-straight-year|title=Maryland misses NIT for second straight year (UPDATE: decline CBI)|date=2012-03-11|work=Testudo Times|access-date=2018-06-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://247sports.com/college/maryland/article/maryland-terrapins-basketball-misses-nit-tournament-invite-116129490/|title=Maryland Terrapins basketball Misses NIT Tournament Invite|work=InsideMDSports|access-date=2018-06-05|language=en-US}}</ref>

===Departures===
On April 6, 2018, freshman forward Bruno Fernando announced he would test the [[2018 NBA draft|NBA draft]], but not sign with an agent.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/terrapins-insider/wp/2018/04/06/maryland-freshman-bruno-fernando-declares-for-nba-draft-but-wont-hire-agent/|title=Maryland freshman Bruno Fernando declares for NBA draft, but won’t hire agent|last=Stubbs|first=Roman|date=2018-04-06|work=Washington Post|access-date=2018-06-04|language=en-US|issn=0190-8286}}</ref> On May 28, he announced he would return to school.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.landof10.com/maryland/bruno-fernando-2018-nba-draft-returns-maryland-basketball|title=Bruno Fernando withdraws from 2018 NBA Draft, returns to Maryland basketball|date=2018-05-28|work=Land of 10|access-date=2018-06-04|language=en-US}}</ref> Sophomore guard [[Kevin Huerter]] declared for the NBA draft on April 20, 2018, but also announced he would not sign with an agent.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2018/04/20/marylands-kevin-huerter-will-declare-for-nba-draft-but-will-not-sign-with-an-agent/|title=Maryland's Kevin Huerter will declare for NBA draft but will not sign with an agent|last=Markus|first=Don|work=baltimoresun.com|access-date=2018-06-04|language=en-US|archive-date=2018-10-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181025133402/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/tracking-the-terps/bs-sp-kevin-huerter-nba-draft-0420-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On May 30, he announced he would stay in the draft and hire an agent, thereby ending his college career.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2018/05/30/marylands-kevin-huerter-decides-to-stay-in-nba-draft-leave-terps-after-sophomore-year/|title=Maryland's Kevin Huerter decides to stay in NBA draft, leave Terps after sophomore year|last=Shaffer|first=Don Markus, Jonas|work=baltimoresun.com|access-date=2018-06-04|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Schedule and results==
The season marked the first time in Big Ten history that the teams played a 20-game conference schedule, setting a precedent for all Division I basketball.<ref name=":02">{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/big-ten-adds-two-games-for-a-20-game-conference-schedule-starting-in-2018-19/|title=Big Ten adds two games for a 20-game conference schedule starting in 2018–19 |last=Norlander|first=Matt|date=October 19, 2017|work=CBS Sports|access-date=March 9, 2018}}</ref> The new schedule also included a regional component to increase the frequency of games among teams in similar areas. Over the course of a six-year cycle (12 playing opportunities), in-state rivals play each other 12 times, regional opponents play 10 times, and all other teams play nine times.<ref name=":02" /> Three in-state series are guaranteed home-and-homes: Illinois and Northwestern, Indiana and Purdue, and Michigan and Michigan State will always play twice.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21076233/big-ten-play-20-game-conference-schedule-next-season|title=Big Ten to move to 20-game conference slate |work=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-03-12}}</ref> The conference opponent list was released on April 19, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041918aae.html|title=2018–19 Conference Season Opponent Breakdown: Teams will compete in 20-game conference schedule, playing seven teams both home and away and six teams once|accessdate=April 19, 2018|date=April 19, 2018|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180420074326/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041918aae.html|archive-date=April 20, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>
